post_topic: CAN-SPAM compliance architecture for agentic email systems
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

Title at top in bold navy text: "Agentic Email Compliance Layer".

The diagram flows left to right across the center of the image in a single horizontal pipeline with three sequential checkpoint gates.

Far left: a rounded rectangle labeled "Agent" with a small robot/gear icon. An arrow points right from Agent.

Checkpoint 1 (leftmost gate): a hexagon labeled "Suppression List Check" in navy. Inside or below the hexagon, a small label reads "Before every send — not at import". A green arrow labeled "Not suppressed" continues right. A red arrow labeled "Halt" points downward from this gate to a red stop-sign shape labeled "Send cancelled".

Checkpoint 2 (center gate): a hexagon labeled "Physical Address Present?" in navy. A small amber callout badge attached to it reads "Fail closed — raises exception". A green arrow labeled "Address valid" continues right. A red arrow labeled "Exception thrown" points downward to a red stop-sign shape labeled "Send blocked — CAN-SPAM violation".

Checkpoint 3 (rightmost gate): a hexagon labeled "HMAC Unsubscribe Token" in navy. A small annotation below reads "Stateless generation / verified on redemption only". A green arrow labeled "Token attached" continues right.

Far right: a rounded rectangle labeled "Email Sent" with a checkmark icon in blue.

Below the main pipeline, a thin horizontal dashed line separates a footnote row. In the footnote row, three small labels in smaller text align beneath their respective checkpoints: "Suppression list checked at send time", "Missing address = hard stop, not warning", "No DB call to generate token".

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text "Kelvin Davis" bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
